To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cyclooxygenase- 2–dependent thromboxane production contributes to basal contractility of isolated rat hearts, that cyclooxygen-ase-2–derived thromboxane production is not involved in the contractile responses to norepinephrine and endothelin-1, and that cyclooxygenas- 2–derived thromoxane production is involved in the contractility of isolated hearts exposed to endotoxin.
the contractile effects of COX-2 are mediated by thromboxane and that the contractility of isolated hearts is not dependent on endogenous COX-2.

the contractility of isolated rat hearts, the effect of cyclooxygenase- 2 inhibition on the contractility of rat hearts, and the role of sphingosine and tumor necrosis factor (TNF) in the contractility of the heart.

COX-2 is a major factor in the pathophysiology of heart failure, but that the effects of COX-2 on the failing heart are not limited to a single mechanism.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cyclooxygenase- 2 (COX-2) pathway is involved in the regulation of myocardial contractility.
the contractility of isolated rat hearts is increased by the cyclooxygenase- 2 inhibitor NS-398, whereas the contractile effects of the cyclooxygen-ase-1 inhibitor indomethacin are less pronounced.
cyclooxygenase (COX) isoenzymes are involved in the regulation of cardiac function, but the exact role of COX-2 in the heart is still not clear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and cyclooxygenase -2 (COX-2) are the two isoforms of cyclooxygenase, an enzyme that catalyzes the formation of prostaglandins from arachidonic acid.
cyclooxygenase- 2 (COX-2) plays an important role in regulating cardiac contractility, which is a key function of the heart.
we have identified a novel mechanism for the regulation of COX-2 activity in the heart.
